stemMd: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Parish registers are a more dependable record of rockfalls than any physical measurement can be.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Raman found that lichen growth rates differ sharply from one boulder to the next.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Lichen size gives a workable estimate of when a rockfall happened, but only for relatively recent falls.

options.label: D
options.textMd: *Rhizocarpon* is the only lichen whose growth rate is steady enough to be measured.

explanationMd:
A main-idea choice has to cover the whole text and claim no more than the text supports.

The passage does three things in order: it introduces lichen size as a clock for rockfalls, it explains why that works (steady outward growth), and it reports what happened when Raman tested it against dated collapses — a close match under about 300 years, and a blur beyond that. Choice C is the only option that carries both halves of the result: the method works, and it has a ceiling.

Two checks worth running on any main-idea answer. First, ask whether the choice would still be true if the last sentence were deleted; if the choice ignores the limitation the text ends on, it is only half the idea. Second, ask whether the text ever makes the comparison the choice makes. Here only Choice C survives both.

distractorRationale.d: This turns a description into an exclusive claim. The text says *Rhizocarpon* grows at a slow, fairly steady rate; it never compares that species with other lichens or calls it the only usable one.
distractorRationale.a: This invents a ranking. The parish registers are used as a known standard to test the lichen method against, not judged more dependable than physical measurement in general.
distractorRationale.b: This misreads the limitation. The estimates bunched together for old falls because lichen growth slows with age, not because different boulders grew lichens at sharply different rates.

accessibilityText: Choose the option that best states the main idea of the passage about using lichen size to date rockfalls.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The text presents lichen size as a rough clock that tracked recorded dates closely for falls under about 300 years but blurred beyond that, which is (c). (a) is never claimed, since the registers serve only as a check. (b) misreads the text: the slowdown is over time, not between boulders. (d) overstates the text with 'only'.

review.notes: Author solved and checked uniqueness: the text's arc is method, mechanism, test, limit, and only B states both the success and the 300-year ceiling.
